paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
authors: Akari Asai; Zeqiu Wu; Yizhong Wang; Aviram Stern; ...
core_problem: Large language models often produce responses with factual inaccuracies due to sole reliance on parametric knowledge. Retrieval-Augmented Generation reduces these issues but indiscriminately retrieving and incorporating a fixed number of passages regardless of necessity or relevance diminishes LM versatility and can lead to unhelpful response generation.
methodology_summary: SELF-RAG trains a single arbitrary LM to adaptively retrieve passages on-demand and to generate and reflect on retrieved passages and its own generations using special reflection tokens. Generating reflection tokens makes the LM controllable during inference, enabling it to tailor behavior to diverse task requirements.
datasets_eval: Open-domain QA, reasoning and fact verification tasks, and long-form generation tasks.
empirical_results: SELF-RAG 7B and 13B significantly outperforms state-of-the-art LLMs and retrieval-augmented models on a diverse set of tasks. Specifically, SELF-RAG outperforms ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat on open-domain QA, reasoning and fact verification tasks, and shows significant gains in improving factuality and citation accuracy for long-form generation.
explicit_limitations: No explicit limitations are provided in the given context.
